headline: South Asia: Pakistan, Turkiye, Saudi Arabia agree to rapid force deployment in the kingdom under Makkah pact
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Pakistan, Turkiye, Saudi Arabia agree to rapid force deployment in the kingdom under Makkah pact.
- Western Russia: One dead and four injured in Russians attack on Kramatorsk – photos.
- Asia: Ukraine attacks Moscow region with 650 drones as both sides step up strikes.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Aboard the USS George Washington, young sailors adjust to war with Iran.
- Military Times, 20 hours ago: Aboard the USS George Washington, young sailors adjust to war with Iran.
Sailors must maintain a ​state of alert and readiness, heightened in the case of the George Washington due to the threat of Iranian attacks.
- Military Times, 20 hours ago: US Army tests counter-drone tech at Mexican border as cartel drone use rises.
The service is seeking to sharpen its defenses against the growing threat of drone use by cartels.
The Caribbean - bottom line: Doctors’ pay fight ends in major win.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 6 hours ago: Doctors’ pay fight ends in major win.
Following the Industrial Disputes Tribunal’s landmark ruling in favour of doctors in their long-running allowances dispute with the State, senior trade unionist Lambert Brown says the medical practitioners are ready to meet with the Government to implement the award. In a quick response on Monday, Brown said the doctors were pleased with the outcome. “We receive the award [ruling] just after 4 p.m. and we can confirm that award is in favour of the doctors and the two issues before the tribunal,” he said.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: One dead and four injured in Russians attack on Kramatorsk – photos.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 5 hours ago: One dead and four injured in Russians attack on Kramatorsk – photos.
Russian FPV drone strikes killed a woman and injured four others, including medical personnel, in targeted attacks on Kramatorsk on 5 October.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 11 hours ago: Moscow comes under large-scale drone attack – photos, videos.
Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin says 650 drones were heading towards Moscow and Moscow Oblast between the evening of 5 October and early 6 October, with 105 reportedly destroyed while approaching the capital.
- Ukrainska Pravda, one hour ago: Russian drone drops explosives in Kherson Oblast, killing man.
A Russian drone dropped explosives near Kachkarivka in Kherson Oblast, killing a man; a woman was also killed in a separate attack the previous day.
- Ukrainska Pravda, one hour ago: Ukrainian forces strike Russian telecommunications hub and UAV and ammunition warehouses.
Units from Ukraine's defence forces struck several Russian military facilities in temporarily occupied Ukrainian territories on 5 October and on the night of 5-6 October.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Kosovo Protesters Against Hague Court Gather Again After Clashes.
- Balkan Insight, one hour ago: Kosovo Protesters Against Hague Court Gather Again After Clashes.
After violent clashes on Monday night, protesters started to reassemble in Pristina to demand legal changes to curb the powers of the Kosovo Specialist Chambers war crimes court following convictions of guerrilla leaders.
- Balkan Insight, 21 hours ago: Kosovo Parliament Moves Towards Changing Law to Curb Hague Special Court.
MPs in first reading adopt major changes to law governing the Hague-based war crimes court following conviction of former Kosovo Liberation Army leaders – although enforcement requires second vote.
- Politico Europe, 3 hours ago: Von der Leyen warns against EU budget cuts.
Commission president dismissed Germany's calls for big savings, arguing that they would undermine EU-wide priorities.
- Balkan Insight, 5 hours ago: From Streets to Polling Stations: Serbia’s Student Movement Takes Electoral Test.
Nearly two years after it was created, Serbia’s student movement is contesting a national election – but experts warn that winning power would only be the start of the challenge.

AFRICA
Africa - bottom line: Ethiopia: PM vows to secure sea access amid fears of return to war.
- Africanews, 14 hours ago: Ethiopia: PM vows to secure sea access amid fears of return to war.
Following almost two weeks of internal conflict that threatens a wider regional war in Ethiopia, the country's prime minister has vowed that government forces are ready to bring a rebel offensive under control.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, just now: Nigeria: NAF Releases Names of 25 Victims Killed in Military Plane Crash [full List].
[Vanguard] The Nigerian Air Force has released the names of 25 people killed in the aircraft crash that occurred in Igbokoda, Ondo State, on Monday.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 5 hours ago: Nigeria: Security Agents Kill ISWAP Commander in Ondo.
[Daily Trust] Security forces in Ondo State have killed Abdussamad Ohida, a commander of the Islamic State West Africa Province, ISWAP.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 8 hours ago: Africa: Military Coups Promise Change - 4 Ways They Can Leave African Countries Worse Off.
[The Conversation Africa] A military coup d'état is the ouster of an elected president or head of state, usually through the use or threat of force. Putschists (those who participate in a coup) often justify their actions by accusing the government of mismanaging the economy and lowering living standards. Political instability is another reason coup makers give for their actions.
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: Wearable counter‑drone tech enters frontline service across US, Ukraine and IDF units.
- Jerusalem Post, 2 hours ago: Wearable counter‑drone tech enters frontline service across US, Ukraine and IDF units.
The wearable counter‑drone kit, deployed by Ukrainian troops and IDF forces and integrated into US Army exercises under EUCOM as top US commander warns troops will be ‘hunted’ by autonomous systems
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 7 hours ago: Mexican and Colombian cartel mercenaries filmed fighting in Ukraine.
Members of Mexican and Colombian cartels are reportedly joining Ukraine’s International Legion to learn drone warfare.
- Jerusalem Post, 13 hours ago: Rabbi Lando: Zionism to blame for Arab hostility, religious IDF troops killed over 'twisted Torah'.
UTJ spiritual leader Lando: '[National-Religious Jews] are being killed because their rabbis teach them twisted Torah' • Litvak rabbi says secular Israelis 'have no connection with Judaism'
- Jerusalem Post, just now: Hamas plotting October 7 attacks on IDF soldiers in Gaza, Israeli intelligence indicates.
Defense Minister Israel Katz: Israel observed intent by Hamas to launch terror attacks on the anniversary of October 7, Hamas and Gazan population will pay "a heavy price beyond all proportion."
South Africa: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Pakistan, Turkiye, Saudi Arabia agree to rapid force deployment in the kingdom under Makkah pact.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 16 hours ago: Pakistan, Turkiye, Saudi Arabia agree to rapid force deployment in the kingdom under Makkah pact.
Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye have agreed to deploy military forces and capabilities rapidly in the kingdom, the Foreign Office (FO) said on Monday following an emergency meeting of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement in Riyadh. The three countries held an emergency meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee (SPDC) of the Makkah Defence Alliance to address the security developments and threats facing Saudi Arabia, the FO statement said.
- The Hindu - International, 17 hours ago: Airstrikes, artillery hit north Ethiopia as government and rebels clash, sources say.
Air attacks killed at least 17 people northwest of Tigray’s capital Mekelle — which federal government forces took over the weekend — according to a bulletin circulated among humanitarian groups
- Dawn (Pakistan), one hour ago: 4 FBR officials, traffic policeman martyred in DI Khan attacks: police.
DERA ISMAIL KHAN: Four Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) officials were martyred in firing by unidentified assailants near Qureshi Mor in Dera Ismail Khan, while a separate attack on a highway traffic police mobile near the Mufti Mahmood Chowk bypass left a police official martyred and another injured, police said on Tuesday. Dera Ismail Khan District Police Officer Ziauddin Ahmad told Dawn that two of the four FBR officials were serving with the board on a contractual basis.
- The Hindu - International, 3 hours ago: Yemen, Saudi Arabia strike Houthis as counteroffensive gets underway.
The Yemeni military said it carried out more than 1,000 strikes and began an offensive against the Houthi-held capital, Sanaa, while the Saudi-led coalition supporting the internationally recognised government said 100 warplanes flew sorties at dawn
Asia - bottom line: Ukraine attacks Moscow region with 650 drones as both sides step up strikes.
- South China Morning Post - China, The Moscow Times, 2 hours ago: Ukraine attacks Moscow region with 650 drones as both sides step up strikes.
A massive attack involving 650 drones targeted Moscow overnight, leaving at least two dead, Russian authorities said on Tuesday. Most of the drones were destroyed by air defences at long range, including 105 intercepted as they approached the capital, Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin wrote on Telegram. Russian state news agency Tass reported it was the second-largest drone attack on the capital region in the past two years. The dead included a 71-year-old man pulled from under the rubble ‌of a house...
- South China Morning Post - China, 2 hours ago: Why India is getting serious about ending the Ukraine war.
India’s recent push to become more involved in helping end the Russia-Ukraine war comes as the costs of the conflict continue to mount for New Delhi, amid the threat of US tariffs on major buyers of Russian energy and a recent drone attack on an Indian-owned pharmaceutical plant in Ukraine. Sunday morning’s drone attack destroyed a large part of Kusum Group’s factory in Sumy, killing one person and injuring several others. The company, which has manufactured generic medicines in Ukraine since...
- South China Morning Post - China, 13 hours ago: Trump says US moved bombers from UK airbase after threats.
US President Donald Trump said on Monday that a threat linked to Iran ⁠had prompted the removal of American B-1 bombers from a British airbase. The planes had been stationed at RAF Fairford, the preferred European base for US bombers, and had recently been used in US strikes on Iran. Last week, five British men were arrested near the base – which Iran’s Revolutionary Guards previously said was a legitimate target – on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts. “We had an idea that there might be a...
- South China Morning Post - China, 6 hours ago: India sizes up US F-35 stealth jets in landmark first on home turf.
US F-35 stealth fighters have joined Indian warplanes for military exercises near the Pakistan border in recent days, marking the first time America’s most advanced multirole combat aircraft has taken part in joint drills in India. The US jets’ participation in the drills “signals a degree of military confidence and interoperability that is difficult to manufacture through communiques”, Sushant Singh, a South Asian studies lecturer at Yale University and former Indian Army officer, told This...
Korean Peninsula - bottom line: North Korea turning to knock-off parts for missiles used in Ukraine: Report.
- NK News, 5 hours ago: North Korea turning to knock-off parts for missiles used in Ukraine: Report.
North Korea has relied heavily on counterfeit U.S. and European parts to produce missiles and drones used in the war against Ukraine, a new report has found, suggesting that sanctions are limiting Pyongyang’s ability to source original components. The U.K.-based Conflict Armament Research (CAR) project analyzed North Korean Hwasong-11-series missiles used by Russia against Ukraine […]
- Yonhap News Agency, just now: N. Korea warns of 'powerful counteraction' if S. Korea intrudes 'even a millimeter' into its territory.
SEOUL, Oct. 6 (Yonhap) -- North Korea on Tuesday warned of an "immediate and pow...
- Yonhap News Agency, 2 hours ago: (LEAD) S. Korea, U.S. aligned on N. Korea policy, denuclearization of Korean Peninsula: FM Cho.
SEOUL, Oct. 6 (Yonhap) -- Foreign Minister Cho Hyun said Tuesday that South Kore...
- NK News, 3 hours ago: Seoul says Ukrainian apology over North Korean POW disclosure falls short.
An apology from Ukraine for publicly disclosing the transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war to South Korea has fallen short of Seoul’s expectations, Foreign Minister Cho Hyun told lawmakers Tuesday. “I cannot say that there was no apology,” Cho said in response to a question from ruling Democratic Party lawmaker Lee Ki-heon during […]
India - bottom line: Saudi-backed Yemen forces claim key Red Sea strait secured.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: Saudi-backed Yemen forces claim key Red Sea strait secured.
In a bold move to counteract Houthi insurgents, Saudi-backed Yemeni military forces have initiated Operation Yemen Dawn, bolstered by a coalition of 100 Saudi fighter jets. The offensive reportedly succeeded in reclaiming significant territories, including the strategic Dhubab airport and Mokha. However, the authenticity of these claims is yet to be independently verified, while the Houthis are challenging the narrative, asserting no losses and launching counterattacks on Saudi positions.
- Times of India - Top Stories, just now: 'Attacks must end': MEA says 11 Indian crew members injured in Hormuz vessel strike.
- Times of India - Top Stories, just now: From US' HACM to India's BrahMos-II: The world's hypersonic arms race heats up.
The US Air Force's Hypersonic Attack Cruise Missile has commenced its flight-test phase in Australia. This program has faced delays, prompting a reduction in overall testing plans to adhere to schedules. Developed alongside the Royal Australian Air Force, it aims for rapid acquisition decisions by 2027. India's hypersonic ambitions are also advancing, recently highlighted by successful testing of a scramjet vehicle.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: flydubai Hero Pilot's Skull Fractured In Attack, Undergoes Emergency Surgery In Saudi.
A depressed skull fracture happens when a skull breaks, and a piece of bone is pushed inward toward the brain. The "fragment" is the broken piece of skull that sits lower than the normal surrounding bone.

AUSTRALIA
Australia - bottom line: Israeli ambassador to Australia says he hopes for return to ‘traditional friendship’ on October 7 anniversary eve.
- The Guardian - Australia, 4 hours ago: Israeli ambassador to Australia says he hopes for return to ‘traditional friendship’ on October 7 anniversary eve.
Relations have soured between the two countries over a number of issues since 2023, but Hillel Newman says a ‘reset’ is possible Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast Israel’s ambassador to Australia says the third anniversary of October 7 is an opportunity for both countries to return to “traditional friendship”. But, in the lead-up to commemorations on Wednesday marking Hamas’ terror attack, leaders of Australia’s Palestinian community say the federal government should do more to help the diaspora suffering since the war on Gaza.
- The Guardian - Australia, 4 hours ago: Australian army soldier killed and five others injured in training exercise in the Northern Territory.
Australian defence force identifies soldier killed in a vehicle rollover near Darwin as Corporal Brendan Hannam • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast Brendan Hannam has been named as the Australian soldier who died in a vehicle rollover during a training accident near Darwin on Monday. Five others were injured. Chief of the army, Lt Gen Susan Coyle, said the incident was a single-vehicle rollover of a troop-carrying vehicle that Hannam was a passenger in. Defence is still investigating. Continue reading...
- ABC News Australia, 6 hours ago: Cross River Rail worker tells inquiry he 'saw red' in brawl with CFMEU members.
A commission of inquiry into the Queensland branch of the CFMEU has heard a group of workers were attacked by union members at a Cross River Rail site in Dutton Park.
- ABC News Australia, 2 hours ago: Australia's 'quite striking' move towards US defies trend.
Mystery still surrounds what happened near UK RAF base Fairford but analysts warn US allies may face seeing their bases targeted.
